about: The origins of a cell are the vertices of a polygon, and what they hold together is its interior.
Two make an edge and no area; three an area; from four a vertex the others do not enclose is an outlier; from five the verdict has a centre, and taking any one origin away leaves it where it was.
As origins are added to one population the meet narrows toward consensus; two populations wearing one name never meet at any number of them.
